title: Ducktective case file
description: The product. One JSON object per line in .ducktective/cases.jsonl, mirrored as Markdown for humans. Field names match skills/ducktective/SKILL.md — that file is the contract, this schema makes it checkable. Unknown keys are rejected: a misspelled field validates, then reads as undefined in the rap sheet.

covered.description: Line sites executed by the failing run; with --baseline, only the ones no passing run touched.

predicted.description: What the check must do if the hypothesis is TRUE. The oracle direction: the check should FAIL (crash, assert wrong) or PASS (behave correctly). run_check.mjs records this so the verdict is arithmetic, not prose.

check_exit_code.description: Exit code of the executed check. null = killed or never started, which can support no verdict.

control.description: Known-good command that must pass for the check to be a valid oracle (SKILL.md rule 5).

probe.description: How the accused location was neutered on a scratch worktree (`raise`/`throw` injected before the line), or null if never probed. The prediction and the control together only prove the check AGREES with the claim; a check that passes for reasons unrelated to the accused line survives both, so this is what makes `confirmed` mean something.

probe_exit_code.description: Exit code of the check with the accused location neutered. null = the probe could not be run.

probe_flipped.description: yes = the check's outcome changed when the accused line was neutered, so the check depends on it. no = it did not change, so the check proved nothing about that line (verdict: inconclusive_vacuous). not-run = never probed.

probe_attempts.description: Per-strategy probe outcomes, e.g. ["delete: artifact (not comparable)", "neutralize: flipped"]. Recorded so the artifact rate is computable from the case file (metric C7) instead of being thrown away.

probe_artifact.description: True when at least one neuter strategy produced a parse/undefined-name artifact rather than a comparable run. Artifacts are not evidence; this is recorded so a high artifact rate is visible.

blind_check.description: The stripped-context re-derivation (design v3 E2), executed by run_check.mjs --blind: a second check the host authors without the first run's context. exit_code is the tool-captured result of running it; a non-reproduction demotes the claim to "unreplicated". Required for every confirmed claim. Honest limit: the tool runs and records the receipt; it cannot prove the second check was authored without context.

check.description: The second, independently written command that was executed.

exit_code.description: Exit code run_check captured for that command.

verified_exit_code.description: Exit code of the re-executed check (run_check --verify).

verified_verdict.description: What the second run would have concluded. Metric #2: a confirmed claim whose verified_verdict differs did not survive.

status.description: `open` exists so a mid-flight case can be persisted; SKILL.md forbids patching from it. A run that never executed is status `unverified` with the harness note in leading_hypothesis — `error` describes the reproduction, not the verdict.

cause_hash.description: Stable identity of the root cause (location + normalised hypothesis + repro command + top frames), derived by writeCase, not typed. Two investigations of the same fault share it, so the store counts recurrence instead of piling near-duplicates.

cause_key.description: The readable identity tuple behind cause_hash, kept for audit.

count.description: How many distinct cases in this repo share this cause_hash. Derived, never hand-typed.

cause_confidence.description: The derived 0..1 cause-confidence, persisted by writeCase so a reader that cannot run the policy still sees the rating. Recomputed from the receipts, never hand-typed.

not_reportable.description: The reason this case may not be surfaced as a finding (status not reportable, or confidence below the floor), or null when it is reportable. Derived by writeCase; the presence of a value is a gate, not a note.

why_violations.description: E5 consistency findings: a `why` or `hypothesis` that cites a file:line appearing nowhere in this case's own stack, covered sites, or candidate locations. Recorded, not refused, so metric C9 can be measured first.
